Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
9 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

tabs.Coverage:
Research conflict Partially resolved
Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Authors should still be contacted for the raw data. C00062
Comparability Limited comparability
At least one observation lacks specimen or conditioning information; no family aggregation performed. C00412
Post-processing / application Evidence recorded

Its own wording is retained: the suggested annealing temperature of models printed with Bambu PC is 85 to 100 °C, and the time is 6 to 12 hours.. 12 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

11 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Impact strength
2 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Research conflict Partially resolved
Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Authors should still be contacted for the raw data. C00062
Comparability Limited comparability
At least one observation lacks specimen or conditioning information; no family aggregation performed. C00412

Charpy strength
12 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
7 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis... polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.
High temperature
Polymer-level reference for PA12, not this product · source: EMS-GRIVORY, Technical Data Sheet Grilon, Grilamid and Grivory – Resistance to Chemicals, p. 3 Hydrolysis resistance PB00209
Hot water or moist air at higher temperatures · limited
Polycondensation products, to which polyamides also belong, have a limited resistance to hot water or moist air at higher temperatures. PA 12 has good hydrolysis resistance compared to other polyamides, but it is gradually molecularly degraded by hot water. Compounds with a high molecular mass will last longer than those with a low molecular mass. Hydrolytic degradation occurs faster in acid media than in neutral or alkaline media. Standard compounds are resistant to pure water to about 70 or 80 °C.

Exposure to short wave light of wavelengths less than 400 nm results in an accelerated decrease in the molecular mass of the polymers, causing molded parts and semi-finished products to become brittle. Light stabilizers, UV absorbers and/or radical scavengers considerably reduce weathering damage. However, the best protection is provided by suitable grades of carbon black, if blackening is possible.

Polycondensation products, to which polyamides also belong, have a limited resistance to hot water or moist air at higher temperatures. Good for

Benefits
“PA612 inherits the best characteristics of both PA6 and PA12, such as toughness and less water absorption.” data sheet, p. 1
“By adding 15 wt.% short carbon fibers with optimized length distribution, mechanical, thermal properties and even surface quality of printed part are all enhanced.” data sheet, p. 1
“After annealing, thermal and mechanical properties are improved further.” data sheet, p. 1
Warping and shrinkage
“After annealing, max. 0.4%-dimensional shrinkage could be observed in Z-axis depending on infill and layer height, no significant dimensional shrinkage in XY-axis.” data sheet, p. 3
Adhesion between layers
“Compared with Raise3D Industrial PA12 CF, it exhibits higher strength-to-weight ratio, better interlayer bonding quality (Z-direction strength) and better dimensional stability.” data sheet, p. 1
Moisture sensitivity
“Dry PA12 CF+ at 80°C for 12 hours before printing, moisture content is crucial for final printed partquality.” data sheet, p. 3
“After drying, we recommend to store PA12 CF+ filaments into Raise3D Filaments Dry Box during theprinting.” data sheet, p. 3
Printing advice
“For a small size model (side length <50 mm), annealing at 80°C for 8 hours is recommended; For a medium-size model (50mm<side length <150 mm), annealing at 80°C for 12 hours is recommended; For a large size model, 100°C for at least 12 hours is recommended.” data sheet, p. 3

Charpy strength
8 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. Hydrolytic stability: not resistant polymer-level M068-hydrolysis
Hot water · not resistant · can screen
All thermoplastic polyester resins will hydrolyze in hot water. The hydrolysis results in polymer degradation and a decrease in the physical properties of the resin. The rate of hydrolysis depends on exposure conditions; primarily time, temperature and the composition of the specific polyester resin. We recommend that parts made from Rynite should not be used in an environment where there is continuous exposure to water at temperatures above 50 °C.

A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Impact strength
4 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Charpy strength
25 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

58 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

58 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Impact strength
4 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

31 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Research conflict Partially resolved
Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Charpy strength
11 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Izod impact strength
9 values

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

12 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Research conflict Partially resolved
Confirmed as a real defect in the source, 2026-09-11, by recomputing the published percentages against the published ultimate strengths: ASA sigma_R 16.82 MPa, so the stated "25 % = 8 MPa" fatigue limit should be 4.2 MPa; PC sigma_R 61.6 MPa, so "7 % = 3.6 MPa" should be 4.3 MPa; PC-ABS sigma_R 52.7 MPa, so "15 % = 4.7 MPa" should be 7.9 MPa. Only PA12 is self-consistent (17 % x 43.4 = 7.4 MPa). The percentage-derived limits and the absolute stresses cannot both be right, so the existing conservative handling stands: retain measured stress and cycle observations only, and continue to reject the percentage-derived limits and the "infinite life" language (a 1e6-cycle run-out is right-censored). Authors should still be contacted for the raw data. C00062

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. Charpy strength
3 values

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

UV and outdoor: limited polymer-level M161-uv-outdoor
UV radiation, unstabilised · stabilised required
Plastics are chemically degraded by the effect of UV radiation. The degree of ageing depends on duration and intensity. In the case of polyurethanes, the effect is seen initially as surface embrittlement. This is accompanied by a yellowing in color and a reduction in mechanical properties. It is possible to improve UV resistance by addition of color pigments which prevent the deep penetration of UV rays... The ageing process can also be delayed by the addition of UV stabilizers.

A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. Impact strength
1 value

Notched impact, Charpy. Only a notched Charpy bar (ISO 179) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Izod is another test on another bar, clamped upright: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Notched impact, Izod. Only a notched Izod bar (ISO 180) in kJ/m², struck at room temperature, is compared. Charpy is another test on another bar, held at both ends: it has its own filter, and the two are never mixed or converted. A value in J/m (ASTM D256) is energy per metre of notch, and one to ASTM D256 printed in kJ/m² is that value converted by its maker with a bar thickness the sheet does not give: neither is an ISO 180 bar. An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

An unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number. All of them stay on record and are shown here.

Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature · limited
All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.

In these 2 categories no source tested this material or its products, so the published behaviour of the neat PET resin is shown instead, from a resin producer's or handbook reference. It is not a test of this grade: fillers, pigments and printing change it. It never passes a requirement; where the reference reports the polymer attacked or dissolved (hydrolytic stability), it screens this material out of that requirement with "Let estimates rule out materials" on, and the SCREENED chip brings it back.
Hydrolytic stability: not resistant polymer-level M067-hydrolysis
Hot water · not resistant · can screen
All thermoplastic polyester resins will hydrolyze in hot water. The hydrolysis results in polymer degradation and a decrease in the physical properties of the resin. The rate of hydrolysis depends on exposure conditions; primarily time, temperature and the composition of the specific polyester resin. We recommend that parts made from Rynite should not be used in an environment where there is continuous exposure to water at temperatures above 50 °C.
Continuous exposure above 50 °C

Outdoor weathering (carbon arc X-W Weather-Ometer, Florida and Arizona exposure) · resistant
Thermoplastic polyester resins rank high, among engineering polymers, for resistance to outdoor weathering... in general, Rynite exhibits good property retention. Overall performance is improved, especially impact strength, by the addition of carbon black (> 0,3 % by weight) to the resin. After 10 000 hours in the X-W Weather-Ometer Rynite 530 NC010 and Rynite 545 NC010 retain over 70 % of their initial tensile strength and 55 % of their original elongation properties.

A value in J/m is energy per metre of notch, and becomes kJ/m² only with the bar's thickness; an unnotched bar absorbs several times the energy, and one whose notch the sheet does not state could be either; a bar struck cold is another number.
